answer: Retrospective behavior-cluster audit. Agents log action traces; an auditor groups accounts by near-duplicate trace similarity, then checks whether each cluster's earliest accounts sit near the activity nadir of their shared launch window. Clusters whose members act in lockstep beyond a crystal of independent timing thresholds get flagged and downweighted. Each identity must sustain distinct, noisy behavior for weeks, and attackers pay per-account compute plus delay, since pruning to avoid the prism of correlation erodes the very output they need.
